title: Prospective Sequential Biosample and Data Collection for the Study of Therapy Resistance in Melanoma (PROSEQ-DYNAMO)
summary: For scientific questions aimed at improving therapeutic response and stratification of therapy in melanoma patients, it is necessary to correlate biosamples collected longitudinally with clinical parameters and clinical outcomes. The investigation of tumor-dynamic processes—especially those that contribute to early therapy resistance in melanoma—will now take place within the framework of the collaborative research project ‘DYNAMO: Immediate tumor dynamics in melanoma therapy’. The expected duration of DYNAMO is 12 years (e.g., in the case of a positively evaluated DFG-SFB funding). The biosample collection strategy for DYNAMO is called PROSEQ and reflects the specific goal of prospectively and sequentially collecting tumor tissue from melanomas, urine, stool, and blood samples, including clinical accompanying data, from patients undergoing oncological systemic therapy and making them available to DYNAMO. PROSEQ itself, as well as the individual research questions and projects of DYNAMO, are evaluated separately by the ethics committee. The biosamples and data collected through PROSEQ are archived and documented in the Essen Department of Dermatology. Sequential sample collection results in a higher burden for patients, which necessitates specific patient information and education.

interventions.name: Biosampling arm under standard systemic therapy for advanced, unresectable melanoma

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Melanoma patients at the Department of Dermatology (stages I to IV according to AJCC 2018) who are capable of giving consent, are scheduled to undergo systemic therapy, and have provided written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients unable to provide informed consent
- Patients under 18 years of age
- Pregnant and breastfeeding women
- Missing or withdrawn consent
